title: Quantum Synchronization
authors: Parvinder Solanki, Albert Cabot, Fernando Iemini, Federico Carollo, Midhun Krishna, Yeshma Ibrahim, Michal Hajdušek, Igor Lesanovsky, Rosario Fazio, Roberta Zambrini, Sai Vinjanampathy
abstract: Natural and engineered classical systems are replete with examples of synchronization, understood as the adjustment of rhythms of physical systems. Such synchronization is at the heart of the stability of several classical technologies, such as mechanical bridges and electrical networks. Given the advent of quantum simulation and computation technologies, it is natural to study a quantum analogue of synchronization and explore novel applications. This review surveys synchronization in few and many-body quantum systems, measures that quantify them, and their applications to quantum technologies.
summary: This review surveys the concept of synchronization, extending established ideas from classical oscillators (like the van der Pol model) to quantum many-body systems. It details various mathematical measures and techniques needed to quantify this phenomenon in open quantum settings. The work is important for understanding stability and coherence in emerging quantum technologies.
main_problem: The review aims to establish a quantum analogue of classical synchronization, which is crucial for understanding stability in both natural and engineered systems.
main_result: Synchronization phenomena can be studied by adapting concepts from nonlinear classical oscillators (like the van der Pol model) into the quantum domain using advanced measurement techniques.
method: The review surveys theoretical methods including analyzing open quantum system dynamics via master equations, phase reduction, and measuring various quantum correlations.
model_or_system: The scope covers synchronization in both few-body and many-body quantum systems. Classical analogies are drawn from self-sustained oscillators (like the vdP oscillator), which require nonlinearity to maintain non-zero steady amplitudes via energy balance ($P_{	ext{gain}} = P_{	ext{diss}}$).
key_observables: Temporal correlations, quantum correlations, phase & frequency locking, and the steady amplitude $A^*$ determined by power balance.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$) and drive strength ($F$), which define parameter regions (Arnold tongues) where synchronization occurs.
main_assumptions: The analysis of entrainment often relies on approximations such as assuming weak non-linearity or slow variation in amplitude and phase to allow for averaging techniques.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the failure of linear systems to sustain oscillations, the existence of stable limit cycles in nonlinear systems (vdP), and parameter diagrams showing regions of frequency locking (Arnold tongues).
paper_structure: The review progresses logically: first introducing classical synchronization concepts, then detailing necessary quantum techniques for study, followed by specific applications across few-body and many-body quantum systems.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant as it bridges nonlinear dynamics from classical physics into the realm of open quantum systems, providing theoretical tools to analyze stability and coherence in complex quantum devices.
